es: Comprobar si una afirmación está respaldada, exagerada o sin evidencia, y distinguir una correlación de una causa.

teaching.en: The claim that sleep improves grades is supported by hard evidence from two schools, so it is safe to repeat it in the report.
teaching.es: La afirmación de que dormir mejora las notas está respaldada por pruebas sólidas de dos colegios, así que es seguro repetirla en el informe.
teaching.explanationEs: Supported by hard evidence: los datos dicen lo mismo que la afirmación, ni más ni menos. Hard evidence son pruebas comprobables.
segments: The claim that sleep improves grades is supported by hard evidence from
two schools, so it is safe to repeat it in the report.
teaching.audioText: The claim that sleep improves grades is supported by hard evidence from two schools, so it is safe to repeat it in the report.

teaching.en: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data show gains for only seven out of ten, so the headline tends to overstate the result.
teaching.es: Decir que todos los estudiantes mejoraron es exagerado: los datos muestran mejoras solo en siete de cada diez, así que el titular tiende a exagerar el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerated: hay datos, pero la frase dice más (every, always, all). Overstate es el verbo: presentar algo como mayor de lo que es.
segments: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data show gains for only
seven out of ten, so the headline tends to overstate the result.
teaching.audioText: Saying that every student improved is exaggerated: the data show gains for only seven out of ten, so the headline tends to overstate the result.

teaching.en: Sports injuries and temperatures rise together in summer, but that is only a correlation, and it does not mean that heat is the cause.
teaching.es: Las lesiones deportivas y las temperaturas suben juntas en verano, pero eso es solo una correlación y no significa que el calor sea la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos cosas que suben a la vez tienen correlación; eso no prueba que una sea la causa (cause) de la otra.
segments: Sports injuries and temperatures rise together in summer, but that is only
a correlation, and it does not mean that heat is the cause.
teaching.audioText: Sports injuries and temperatures rise together in summer, but that is only a correlation, and it does not mean that heat is the cause.

teaching.en: Unlike last year, when attendance fell in every month, this year it rose, so the old explanation no longer seems to hold up.
teaching.es: A diferencia del año pasado, cuando la asistencia bajó todos los meses, este año subió, así que la vieja explicación ya no parece resistir.
teaching.explanationEs: Unlike + sustantivo o expresión de tiempo contrasta dos situaciones; hold up dice que una explicación sigue siendo válida ante los datos.
segments: Unlike last year, when attendance fell in every month, this year it
rose, so the old explanation no longer seems to hold up.
teaching.audioText: Unlike last year, when attendance fell in every month, this year it rose, so the old explanation no longer seems to hold up.

teaching.en: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas boys' teams grew by only 3 percent, so the two groups should not be described in the same way.
teaching.es: Los equipos de chicas crecieron un 12 %, mientras que los de chicos crecieron solo un 3 %, así que no deberían describirse de la misma manera.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereas une dos cláusulas completas que se contrastan; se puede usar while en su lugar.
segments: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas boys' teams grew by only 3
percent, so the two groups should not be described in the same way.
teaching.audioText: Girls' teams grew by 12 percent, whereas boys' teams grew by only 3 percent, so the two groups should not be described in the same way.

teaching.en: The figures suggest that training time matters, but a careful reader will not draw a conclusion about the cause from one survey on its own.
teaching.es: Las cifras sugieren que el tiempo de entrenamiento importa, pero un lector cuidadoso no sacará una conclusión sobre la causa a partir de una sola encuesta por sí sola.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest es un verbo prudente: apunta a una relación sin afirmar que esté demostrada; draw a conclusion es sacar conclusiones, y on its own significa «por sí solo».
segments: The figures suggest that training time matters, but a careful reader will not
draw a conclusion about the cause from one survey on its own.
teaching.audioText: The figures suggest that training time matters, but a careful reader will not draw a conclusion about the cause from one survey on its own.

prompt.es: Lee el informe y elige el veredicto para: «Todos los alumnos mejoraron tras dormir más.»

choices.text: Exaggerated: 140 of the 200 improved, but sixty saw no change.
Supported: the survey found gains among students who slept longer.
Unsupported: the survey says nothing about marks after more sleep.

feedback.es: Mejoraron 140 de 200, el 70 %, y 60 no notaron cambio: decir que todos mejoraron exagera los datos.

hint.es: Compara la palabra every de la afirmación con los 140 de 200 del informe.

origin.text: Extract from the school report: 'In a survey of 200 students, 140 said that their marks improved after they started sleeping eight hours a night. The other 60 saw no change in their marks.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Eso es una correlación, no una causa: el verdadero motivo es el calor.»

feedback.es: Dos cosas que suben juntas tienen una correlación; el calor es la causa real de ambas, no una de la otra.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo para dos datos que suben a la vez, sin que uno cause al otro.

origin.text: Ice-cream sales and swimming accidents both rise in July. That is a ___, not a cause: the real reason for both is the hot weather.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las cifras sugieren un vínculo, pero no prueban la causa.»

answer.text: The figures suggest a link but they do not prove the cause

feedback.es: Suggest apunta a una relación posible; do not prove deja claro que la causa no está demostrada.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto: las cifras.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye la presentadora sobre el curso de tutorías.

choices.text: That it had no effect at all on the marks of the students.
That its real effect is much smaller than the press release suggests.
That the press release understated how much the marks had risen.

feedback.es: El grupo sin tutorías también subió un 6 %, así que el programa explica solo dos puntos de los ocho que presume el comunicado.

origin.audio: A radio host is reading a press release: Our new tutoring course has changed results, and marks rose by eight percent this year. Then she checks the table. Marks did rise in the tutored group, but they also rose by six percent in the group without tutoring, so the course itself accounts for only two points.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de contraste o de pruebas con su traducción.

pairs.es: A diferencia del norte, el oeste perdió socios.

pairs: The north added members, whereas the west lost them.

pairs.es: El norte sumó socios, mientras que el oeste los perdió.

pairs: The study does not hold up against new data.

pairs.es: El estudio no resiste los datos nuevos.

pairs: The claim is supported by hard evidence.

pairs.es: La afirmación está respaldada por pruebas sólidas.

feedback.es: Unlike introduce un sustantivo, whereas una cláusula completa; hold up y hard evidence hablan de la solidez del dato.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por tanto, el titular parece exagerar el resultado.»

feedback.es: Pasar de 40 a 32 minutos no es reducir a la mitad: el titular overstate el resultado, es decir, lo exagera.

origin.text: The newspaper says that the new bus lane 'cut journey times by half'. The council's table shows a fall from 40 to 32 minutes. The headline therefore seems to ___ the result.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura adopta la lectora ante la propuesta del director.

choices.text: She agrees that the menu must go to every school at once.
She rejects the whole claim because she thinks the figures are unreliable.
She would test the menu elsewhere before using it everywhere.

feedback.es: La lectora no rechaza la afirmación ni la acepta sin más: pide una prueba en un segundo colegio antes de sacar conclusiones.

origin.audio: The canteen report says that since the new menu started, attendance at afternoon lessons has risen by five percent. The director is happy and wants to bring the menu to other schools. But the reader who checked the table is more careful. During the same months, the school also changed its timetable, and a winter illness that kept students away came to an end. She says the figures fit the claim, but they cannot show that the menu is the cause. She recommends a trial in a second school before anyone draws a conclusion.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué la lectora menciona la enfermedad y el horario.

choices.text: Because other changes could also explain the rise in attendance.
Because the illness made the new menu look worse than it was.
Because they prove that the menu had no effect on attendance.

feedback.es: El cambio de horario y el fin de una enfermedad son otras explicaciones posibles: por eso la tabla no prueba que el menú sea la causa.

origin.audio: The canteen report says that since the new menu started, attendance at afternoon lessons has risen by five percent. The director is happy and wants to bring the menu to other schools. But the reader who checked the table is more careful. During the same months, the school also changed its timetable, and a winter illness that kept students away came to an end. She says the figures fit the claim, but they cannot show that the menu is the cause. She recommends a trial in a second school before anyone draws a conclusion.

prompt.es: Completa: «Las ventas subieron un 30 % en el centro, mientras que bajaron en los pueblos.»

feedback.es: Whereas une dos cláusulas completas que contrastan: subida en el centro, bajada en las afueras.

origin.text: Sales of electric bikes rose by 30 percent in the city centre, ___ they fell slightly in the villages. The shop owner says that location matters more than price.

prompt.es: Elige el veredicto para: «Las obras del gimnasio causaron la caída de la piscina.»

choices.text: Supported: both falls happened in the month when the gym closed.
Not proven: the report shows two falls together, not a cause.
Exaggerated: the report says that pool attendance fell only slightly.

feedback.es: El informe solo muestra que las dos caídas coincidieron en julio; eso es una correlación, no una causa demostrada.

origin.text: From the clinic's report: 'Among the 400 members who joined the gym in January, 300 were still attending in June. Attendance at the gym and at the swimming pool both fell in July, when the gym closed for repairs for two weeks.'

prompt.es: Lee la nota del lector y elige qué da a entender sobre el titular.

choices.text: That it is fair, since journey times did fall after the lanes opened.
That the council's table contradicts itself, so nothing can be concluded.
That it makes a small change in journey times sound big.

feedback.es: La tabla muestra una bajada de solo tres minutos, y el titular habla de acabar con los atascos: lo exagera.

origin.text: Reader's note: the headline says 'Bike lanes end traffic jams'. Yet the council's table, quoted lower down, shows that journey times on the main road fell from 34 to 31 minutes after the lanes opened, and that the road is still busy at eight.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la estudiante sobre la conclusión de su amigo.

choices.text: That it claims more than the report can support.
That it is reasonable, but the report should have used more students.
That it is wrong because phone use has no link with sleep.

feedback.es: La estudiante dice que el informe solo halló un vínculo, así que la conclusión de su amigo va más allá de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.audio: A student is talking about a report on phone use. The report says that students who use their phones late sleep less. My friend says that proves phones spoil sleep, but I disagree. Maybe stressed students both use their phones and sleep badly. The report only found a link, so his conclusion goes further than the data allow.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus autores se niegan a sacar una conclusión sobre el té en sí.»

feedback.es: La colocación es draw a conclusion (o reach a conclusion): hay otro factor, la riqueza, que explicaría ambos datos.

origin.text: The survey found that people who drink tea live longer. Its authors, however, refuse to ___ a conclusion about tea itself, because richer people may drink more tea and also live longer.
